small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_HW tiles (e.g. 1024) with BLOCK_OC=8/16 since C_IN_C=8 is tiny — the inner K-loop is only 72 iterations, so favor wide spatial tiles to amortize weight loads; sweep num_warps∈{4,8,16}, num_stages∈{2,3,4}.
- Hoist the weight load out of the spatial dimension: precompute the full `w_tile[BLOCK_OC, C_IN_C*KH*KW]` once via `tl.load` with broadcast indices, then in the kh/kw/ic loop just reuse the register-resident weight slice — avoids 72 separate masked loads per program.
- Pre-pad output W_OUT to a multiple of BLOCK_HW (or use 2D tiling on (oh, ow) instead of flattened hw) to eliminate the modulo/divide on offs_hw and improve coalescing of x loads.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an implicit-GEMM with K = C_IN*KH*KW = 72 as the inner reduction axis and use `tl.dot` on (BLOCK_M=BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N=BLOCK_HW) tiles — current kernel does scalar FMAs via broadcast outer products, leaving tensor cores idle. Pad K to 128 and use fp16/tf32 accumulation into fp32 via `tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)`.
- Switch to NHWC (channels-last) input layout so the GEMM-K dimension (C_IN×KH×KW) is contiguous in memory; do a one-time permute of weight to (KH,KW,C_IN,C_OUT) and of x to (N,H,W,C_IN), then im2col gather is a coalesced vector load along C_IN per (kh,kw).
- Fuse the bias-subtract-Mish epilogue on the `tl.dot` accumulator before the store (already done), and consider a persistent-CTA design that walks multiple (oh,ow) output tiles per program to reuse the loaded weight tile across the spatial axis.
